subject: Aligning engagement platform licenses and pilot consolidation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Engagement tooling — proposal to consolidate pilot licenses

Hi Laura / Rishi —

Quick note to kick off a short procurement run for our sales engagement tools. With the Q4 ramp and multiple pilots running (Outreach and Salesloft), I want to propose we consolidate near-term pilots under a single vendor to simplify onboarding and forecasting. The ask: get commercial terms and a pilot consolidation quote from Outreach first, then compare to Salesloft if numbers diverge materially.

Objectives:
- Reduce duplicate seat spend across pilots by ~25% for Q3/Q4 forecast
- Standardize on one sequence engine for SDR/AE workflows during the enterprise pilot
- Keep renewal alignment simple (one invoice path, single PO)

Laura — can you surface current license counts and any outstanding PO constraints? Rishi — can procurement/finance advise on preferred contract cadence (annual vs. 12-mo commit) and where discounts need legal sign-off?

I’ll reach out to Outreach for an initial consolidation quote and ask them to include a short migration checklist. If Outreach is within 10% of Salesloft on net unit economics we should prefer the simpler migration.

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Attached is a quick headcount snapshot across SDR, AE pilots, and existing Outreach seats. Key notes:
- Current active seats (pilot + standard): SDR 42, AE 18, CS (light) 6.
- Renewal windows: ~40% of Outreach seats renew in Nov; Salesloft renewals staggered Jan–Mar.
- Two teams have strong sequences built in Outreach (SDR core), Salesloft primarily used by an outbound AE pod.

I flagged vendor contacts and a PO lock for one enterprise account that forces 30-day notice for license swaps. We should surface that to vendor conversations.

Attaching the projection you referenced.

Hi Marissa / Laura —

Thanks for the context. Attached is a consolidated pilot quote we put together based on your headcount sheet and the objectives you outlined. Highlights:
- Consolidated pilot pricing assumes a 12-month pilot with a credit for migration training + data-mapping (one-time).
- Net unit economics are ~8% below your combined current spend when accounting for the migration credit.
- We included a phased migration checklist (export > canonicalization > import > QA) and a recommended roll-out for SDR -> AE -> CS.

Files attached: Outreach_Consolidation_Quote_20260816.pdf, migration_checklist.md

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the finance/ops team through the line items.

Best,

Marissa —

Thanks for the ping. Quick answers:
- Invoice credit: Finance is OK with milestone-based credits (we’ll map milestones to implementation acceptance). Please ask Outreach to label the credit in the quote as "Implementation Credit (milestone-driven)" and include a short acceptance checklist.
- PO lock: Procurement expects a 30-day notice window for moving seats tied to that customer. We can include a clause that sequencing for those seats requires written confirmation from the impacted account team.
- Contract cadence: prefer a 12-month pilot term with monthly invoicing to keep cashflow flexible. If Outreach needs annual prepay for discounting, please have them show both pricing lines.

Next step: Ben, can you review Outreach's standard SOW once we receive it and flag any non-standard IP/data clauses?

Rishi
Director, Procurement
Redwood Inference
